answers.core:
Yes. Code protection is a fundamental concern for any developer distributing games publicly.
External tools are unreliable, version-dependent, and can break across engine updates.
A core, engine-level implementation ensures consistent functionality, compatibility with future Godot releases, and trust that developers’ intellectual property remains secure.
answers.workaround: No. While simple renaming scripts could be written, they cannot reliably handle all bytecode, type, and reference cases without breaking the game. A robust solution must be integrated into the engine’s export pipeline to ensure full compatibility and maintain stability.

title: Built-in GDScript Obfuscation System for Better Game Source Protection
